newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to disclose Jewish assets deal with Swiss.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to disclose Jewish assets deal with Swiss.

text.p: Hungary said on Wednesday it would publish details shortly of a secret deal between the Hungarian and Swiss governments to transfer assets to Hungary from accounts held by Jewish holocaust victims.

Marta Fekszi, deputy head of the Hungarian Foreign Ministry's department of international law told the Budapest daily Nepszabadsag the 1973 protocol, kept in the archives of the ministry, would be made public "within a few days".
"The exact date of publication is a matter of the ongoing negotiations with the Swiss authorities," she said.

According to Hungarian foreign ministry sources Switzerland and Hungary concluded a confidential protocol in 1973 by which Switzerland transferred 325,000 Swiss francs ($259,200) from bank deposits of Jews who perished in World War Two to the Hungarian government.
The protocol was attached to inter-state property and war-time compensation agreements concluded in 1950 and 1973.
Foreign ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said talks with the Swiss government centre on what to do with the funds.

"The (assets) could be returned but before that we have to check the relevant documents," he said. "It's complicated because many of the assets are held in Switzerland and are categorised by the Swiss as of 'unclaimed ownership'," he said.
"We also have to agree with the Swiss government on publishing a protocol which both parties agreed originally would remain confidential," he added.

Switzerland, pressed by foreign critics, pledged on Tuesday to answer by December 4 accusations that it used the wealth of Holocaust victims to compensate Swiss citizens for property seized in eastern Europe.
Szentivanyi said Hungary concluded 20 property rights agreements in the late 1940s and early 1950s with 17 Western countries.

The accords dealt with the payment of war reparations by Hungary, a World War Two ally of Nazi Germany, as well as compensation for Western-owned property nationalised by the Communist government which took power in 1949.

Some 600,000 of Hungary's 800,000 Jews perished in Nazi labour or concentration camps. There are an estimnated 100,000 Jews in Hungary today, including 20,000 Holocaust survivors. ($1=1.2540 Swiss Franc)
